docs.title: Footy Scan Documentation
docs.text: Welcome to the Footy Scan documentation! This documentation will help you understand, use, and contribute to the Footy Scan project.

docs.title: What is Footy Scan?
docs.text: Footy Scan is an application that: - Tracks players and objects in football match videos - Applies ML-based object detection and tracking - Produces time-accurate structured data for analytics - Supports both file-based and live stream inputs

docs.title: Getting Started

docs.text:
# Install the package
uv pip install -e .

# Install ML dependencies
uv pip install "torch" "opencv-python" "tqdm"

# Run the entry point

docs.title: Agent Guidelines
docs.text:
Rea# Agent and Tooling Guidelines

This repository includes a short developer guideline for automated agents and maintainers who run programmatic edits.

  • Always check available tools and the MCP/context before making automated changes.
  • Verify which tool APIs (for example: file editors, search, terminal) are available in your environment.
  • Confirm access and permissions for any remote services or repos you'll interact with.
  • When converting or processing data, prefer using the repository's docs/timings.md and docs/pipeline_architecture.md for canonical time and pipeline conventions.
  • Ensure any automated edits preserve existing content by reading files first and applying minimal, well-documented changes.
  • Include a brief explanation of edits in commit messages or pull request descriptions.

These guidelines are intended to reduce accidental changes and help maintain consistent behaviour when using automated coding agents against this codebase.

docs.title: Docs
docs.text:
• Read How to contribute to the docs before you change any page.
  • Every change updates the docs in the same PR. If your change makes a page wrong, fix the page.
  • Use plain language and Mermaid diagrams, following that guide.
  • Run the docs build and look at a screenshot of every diagram you add or change.
  • Never put secrets, private hostnames, IP addresses or private bucket names in docs. The site is public.
  • When a TODO item starts, moves or finishes, update docs/todo.md.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text: Every agent and contributor must run make check (or have the pre-commit hook installed with make hooks) before committing. Never use --no-verify to skip the hooks. If you could not run a check (for example the machine cannot run the tests), say so in the commit message or PR description and name the check. See Checks before you commit.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
footy-track is a three-stage video analysis pipeline: detect → track → extract. Each stage is independent and replaceable. Data flows forward through the stages as Pydantic models, all carrying a canonical ContinuousTime timestamp.

Video
  │
  ▼
InputConsumer          ← decodes frames, stamps with GameTime + metadata
  │
  ▼
BroadcastClassifier    ← gates: is this frame worth processing?
  │ (Yes frames only)
  ▼
ObjectDetector         ← finds players, ball, referee, coach, substitutes
  │
  ▼
Tracker                ← links detections across frames → persistent IDs
  │
  ▼
EventExtractor         ← infers passes, shots, tackles from trajectories
  │
  ▼
OutputProducer         ← writes JSON / CSV / API

docs.title: Stage 0 — Broadcast Classification (gate)
docs.text:
Before running object detection (which is expensive), each frame is classified as pitch view (Yes) or non-pitch (No). Replays, crowd shots, and graphics overlays are filtered out.

Why: Object detection on a replay or close-up face shot wastes compute and produces garbage detections. Filtering first keeps the output clean and speeds up batch processing significantly.

How: A fine-tuned YOLO classification model (yolo11n-cls) returns BroadcastClassification(label, confidence). The model is trained on a binary No/Yes dataset and achieves ~98% top-1 accuracy on a binary val set.

Key decision: The classifier runs on every frame and is cheap. Only Yes frames advance to detection.

docs.title: Stage 1 — Object Detection
docs.text:
Locates objects in each frame and returns normalized bounding boxes.

Why YOLO: Fast enough for real-time use, fine-tunable on domain data, well-supported via Ultralytics. YOLO11 (the current generation) offers strong accuracy/speed tradeoffs at multiple model sizes.

Why domain fine-tuning: A COCO-trained model knows "person" and "sports ball" but cannot distinguish player from coach from referee from substitute. Fine-tuning on Roboflow-labelled match footage produces a 7-class model covering the roles that matter for football analytics.

Two implementations: - UltralyticsObjectDetector — YOLO-based, fast, good for player/ball detection. - UltralyticsSam3Detector — SAM 3 segmentation, text-prompted per category. Slower but handles ambiguous cases (in-play vs. out-of-play ball) by specifying natural-language prompts with per-prompt confidence thresholds. Derives bounding boxes from masks with optional padding; uses centre-distance NMS to suppress duplicates.

Coordinate convention: All boxes are stored as normalized [x, y, w, h] (top-left origin, values in [0, 1]). This keeps the schema resolution-independent and simplifies downstream use.

docs.title: Stage 2 — Tracking
docs.text:
Associates detections across frames to assign persistent object IDs.

Why: A sequence of per-frame bounding boxes with no identity is not useful for event inference. Tracking turns "there is a player at (0.3, 0.5)" into "player #7 moved from (0.3, 0.5) to (0.35, 0.52) over the last 10 frames."

How (planned): Hungarian algorithm assignment using the lap library, matching detections between frames by IoU overlap. This is a well-understood, fast approach for single-camera tracking.

Current state: Not yet implemented as a standalone module. Detection output is consumed frame-by-frame. Tracking is the next major pipeline stage to build.

docs.title: Stage 3 — Event Extraction (planned)
docs.text:
Infers higher-level match events from tracked trajectories: passes, shots, tackles, set-pieces, substitutions.

Why separate from tracking: Events are emergent — a pass is not visible in any single frame but in the trajectory of the ball and proximate players over time. Keeping event extraction downstream of tracking lets the tracker stay simple.

Approach: Rule-based or learned classifiers over tracked trajectory windows. Not yet implemented.

docs.title: Time handling
docs.text:
Two time systems exist in football video:

  • GameTime — the referee/broadcast clock. Resets at each half. Available from video metadata.
  • ContinuousTime — seconds from first-half kickoff, never resets. This is the canonical format for all stored records.

Conversion requires GameMetadata (specifically half_start_continuous: the ContinuousTime at which the second half kicked off, which accounts for first-half stoppage time).

Key decision: All output records carry ContinuousTime, not GameTime. This means downstream consumers never need to know match structure to align or merge observations.

docs.title: Dataset and training
docs.text:
Roboflow manages labelled datasets for both the detection model and the classifier. Labels are created via Roboflow's annotation tools and versioned as datasets. The pipeline includes upload scripts (labelling.py, scripts/upload_*.py) to push frames from inference runs back into Roboflow for active learning.

Weights & Biases tracks all training runs (hyperparameters, metrics, model artifacts). Run history is documented in docs/training/notable_runs.md.

Training scripts (scripts/train_object_detector.py, scripts/train_classifier.py) handle Roboflow download, model fine-tuning, and W&B logging. They accept a DATA_ROOT env var and an optional --local-dataset flag to bypass the download.

docs.title: Key design decisions
docs.text: Decision Rationale Broadcast classifier first Cheap gate eliminates non-pitch frames before expensive detection Normalized bounding boxes Resolution-independent; no pixel math in the schema layer ContinuousTime is canonical Downstream consumers don't need to know match structure Pluggable detector interface Swap YOLO for SAM3 (or anything else) without touching the rest of the pipeline Pydantic data models Validated, serializable, IDE-friendly — the schema is self-documenting lap for tracking Fast, well-tested Hungarian assignment library; no ML overhead for tracking Metaflow for batch jobs Orchestrates large-scale processing (e.g., a full season) with retry and parallelism

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Reviewed against main @ 26d2506, 2026-11-08. Where a doc and the code disagree, this page follows the code. Open work is in the TODO list; measured numbers are in Best pipeline and label needs; datasets are in Datasets and labels.

Every number has a source next to it (a file, a results file, a commit, or a knowledge-base page written KB:<page>; the knowledge base is the author's private notes and is not in this repo). A number with no artifact behind it is unverified; one from a superseded setup is superseded. Stages with no working method are UNSOLVED. "Wired" means a script or server path actually reaches the code.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text:
footy-track turns broadcast football video into ball and player data. Today it is a set of scripts run by hand plus one FastAPI labelling server. There is no orchestrator (metaflow/docker/Dockerfile exists, no flow is defined).

  1. A classifier cuts the match into broadcast-only shot clips.
  2. RT-DETR-L runs on every frame and writes machine labels (tier 3).
  3. Humans label and review in the labeller, writing GT sidecars (tier 1 and 2).
  4. GT sidecars and Roboflow sets go into a DuckDB feature store, which exports a by-clip YOLO dataset for training.
  5. Serving, projection to the pitch, event extraction and output are scaffolds that nothing calls.

Two facts shape everything below:

  • The machine-labelled corpus is one match. All 162 clips in machine_labels/ are arsenal_mancity_20250925 (docs/design/player_reid.md section 0, M7). No corpus-level number has been shown to generalise across matches.
  • The production inputs are not in git. The RT-DETR training command, the batch inference script, the machine-labels to ball-candidates filter and the clip-alias symlinks live outside the repo (T-09).

Provenance tiers: labeller is tier 1 (human), vittrack plus the human_checked tag is tier 2, anything machine-only is tier 3. What each tier means for training, and how a label reaches the trainer, is in Datasets and labels.

docs.title: 5.1 Labeller
docs.text:
One FastAPI app, src/footy_track/labeller/server.py. Its canonical spec is src/footy_track/labeller/README.md (requirements LAB-nnn, linked to tests); it is outside docs_dir, so it is not published here.

Page What it does State /labeller Hand-mark boxes, propagate with VitTrack over a WebSocket run Works mechanically. For the ball, Run halts at frame 1 (confidence 0.119 against the 0.30 handback in video_utils.py:51,55). This is the safe behaviour: lowering the threshold would write off-ball boxes into GT. /object_review Grid and modal crop review, edit, re-run the detector Works. /ball_check Phone-sized yes/no and drag-to-correct on RT-DETR ball candidates (356,812 over 162 clips), confidence-stratified (one card in four is uniform; the rest are weighted towards the borderline window), event dedupe Works. Its verdicts reach nothing downstream (T-02); see Ball Check. /identity, /identity/merge Tracklet purity, jersey grounding, pairwise merges Human side only. /ingest Clip ingestion Returns 500: labeller/web/ingest.html is missing (server.py:160-162, T-18).

Gotcha: review._parse_jsonl_box reports vittrack boxes as provenance labeller (OPEN-3, pinned by tests), so filter on tags, not on that field (KB:footy-labeller-gotchas).

docs.title: Ball Check: verdicts, corrections and undo
docs.text:
Who this is for: anyone changing /ball_check or wondering why its work does not show up in a training set. Code: labeller/ball_check.py, labeller/web/ball_check.html.

flowchart LR
  classDef code fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#111
  classDef data fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#6b7280,color:#111
  classDef dead fill:#fee2e2,stroke:#dc2626,color:#111
  classDef bc fill:#ede9fe,stroke:#7c3aed,color:#111

  CARD["Card: crop of one<br/>detector box"]:::bc
  SWIPE["ball, not_ball,<br/>box_off, unsure"]:::bc
  DRAG["Drag a new box<br/>= corrected"]:::bc
  UNDO["Undo"]:::bc
  POSTV["POST /verdict"]:::code
  SAVE["POST /save_box"]:::code
  POSTU["POST /undo"]:::code
  VLOG[("ball_checks/<clip>.jsonl<br/>append-only, last line wins")]:::data
  SC[("ball_gt_marks/<clip>.jsonl<br/>tag labeller")]:::data
  QUEUE["Queue and /stats:<br/>hide judged cards,<br/>re-estimate boundary,<br/>precision tallies"]:::code
  ING["ingest_gt<br/>top-level files only"]:::code
  LOST["Feature store,<br/>export, training"]:::dead

  CARD --> SWIPE --> POSTV --> VLOG
  CARD --> DRAG --> SAVE --> SC
  DRAG -- "then verdict corrected" --> POSTV
  CARD --> UNDO --> POSTU -- "null tombstone" --> VLOG
  VLOG --> QUEUE
  VLOG -. "never read" .-> LOST
  SC --> ING --> LOST

Legend: purple is the Ball Check path, blue is code in git, grey is data, red is where the work stops. The diagram shows that a yes or no only reaches the verdict log, a dragged box reaches the sidecar and so can reach training, and undo touches only the log.

  • Verdicts. One JSON line per decision: clip, frame_index, box_index, source (cand for a detector candidate, sidecar for a box already in a sidecar), confidence, bbox, label, provenance, corrected_bbox, ts. There are five verdicts: ball, not_ball, box_off (the ball is there but the box is wrong), corrected and unsure. The last line for a (source, clip, frame, box) wins.
  • Corrections. Dragging a box calls save_box first, then logs a corrected verdict. For a candidate (the usual case, because candidate clips mostly have no sidecar) save_box appends a new tier 1 line [label, labeller] to <clip>.jsonl, creating the file under the clip name the card shows. For a sidecar box it rewrites that box in place through the review endpoint, and falls back to appending if that fails.
  • Undo. Appends a line with verdict: null (a tombstone) and puts the card back in the queue. It does not revert a box that save_box wrote, and correcting the card again appends a second box (T-05).
  • What reads verdicts today. Only the queue and /ball_check/stats. The queue hides judged cards and re-estimates its sampling boundary, starting at 0.25, as the confidence where measured precision crosses 0.5. The stats endpoint reports precision as (ball + box_off + corrected) over those plus not_ball, and clean_precision without box_off. The precision bands counted only ball and corrected; there are no box_off verdicts in the 364, so the two agree.
  • What does not. ingest_gt only globs top-level *.jsonl, so ball_checks/ is never imported, and the export keeps not_ball boxes that sit in a sidecar as positives (T-02, seam S2).

docs.title: 5.2 Feature store
docs.text:
DuckDB. Tables game, frame, detection, track_meta, run; views frame_features, detections_enriched, tracks_enriched. Detection key is (game_id, source, run_id, frame_index, detection_id) (schema.py:301). The canonical flag arbitrates per run group, not per row (schema.py:19-71 docstring); all gt_import_* runs of a clip form one group (schema.py:40-48). Importers cover Roboflow YOLO sets (hand_label), labeller/SAM3 JSON and GT sidecars (ingest_gt.py). export_training_dataset.py writes a by-clip train/val[/test] split excluding eval clips, tested in tests/feature_store/. Parquet export exists (store.py:270-326) but no workflow uses it; DuckDB is primary. game_id is a clip stem for GT imports (ingest_gt.py:202,227), not a match.

What is and is not in the store, and a diagram of its keys, is in Feature store design, section 7.1. detection_id is positional (importers.py:228, ingest_gt.py:199); the content-hash fix in identity/stable_id.py is never called. difficulty.py is never called.

docs.title: 5.3 Training
docs.text:
• scripts/train_object_detector.py pulls Roboflow footy-track-detection or a --local-dataset. Several defaults are traps (--imgsz 640, --device mps, --dataset-version 3, --workers 8, --cache ram); the table is in Training, defaults that are traps (T-06). It includes an MPS assigner workaround (209f1bb).
  • The RT-DETR-L training command that made the production checkpoint is not in any branch.
  • scripts/optuna_sweep_object_detector.py and train_classifier.py are older and unverified.
  • .dvc/config:4 points at a macOS path (a home-directory path).
  • The Vast.ai scripts KB:vast-ai-gpu-rental describes (scripts/vast/*.sh) are not in main or any remote branch (checked 2026-10-25).

docs.title: 6. Data formats that cross stage boundaries
docs.text:
There are six ball and box label formats and no module owns them:

  1. Labeller sidecar ball_gt_marks/<stem>.jsonl: bbox and center as dicts, tags = [label, provenance, *markers]. Written by session._box_line (session.py:309-317), review_correct (review.py:335-344) and ball_check._append_gt (ball_check.py:713-720). Read by session, review, ball_check, ingest_gt and build_eval_sidecars.py, each with its own parser. Skip markers: {bbox: null, tags: ["no_ball" | "not_broadcast"]}.
  2. Sparse centre GT (scripts/label_ball_centers.py): center as a [x, y] list.
  3. Eval sidecar eval_data/clips/<stem>.jsonl (ball_eval/dataset.py): one row per frame, list bbox and center.
  4. Machine labels and candidates: dict bbox, plus confidence, model_id, run_id, reviewed, tags = [label, "rtdetr"].
  5. Verdict log ball_checks/<stem>.jsonl: {clip, frame_index, box_index, source, confidence, verdict, bbox, label, provenance, corrected_bbox, ts}. Verdicts are ball, not_ball, box_off, corrected, unsure; undo appends a verdict: null tombstone.
  6. Tracklets JSONL and identity label logs.

docs.title: Which reader accepts which format
docs.text:
The parsers disagree. A list bbox is [x, y, w, h]; a dict bbox is {x, y, w, h}. A centre-only row has bbox: null and a center. The table is read from the code on main, 2026-11-08; "TypeError" means the line indexes a list as a dict and raises.

Reader Code Dict bbox List bbox Centre-only row Unknown class tag becomes Labeller session (load) session._restore_box_line yes yes ignored on load, so the next flush rewrites the file without it in_play_ball Object review review._parse_jsonl_box yes yes ignored player Ball Check sidecar boxes ball_check._sidecar_ball_boxes yes yes ignored skipped (not a ball) Ball Check candidates candidates.read_candidates yes TypeError (:239) ignored skipped (ball tags only) Candidate embedder scripts/embed_ball_candidates.py yes TypeError in describe ignored skipped (ball tags only) Feature store ingest ingest_gt.ingest_gt_jsonl yes TypeError at :210, which aborts the whole ingest dropped; the frame is still recorded the raw tag becomes the label Player tracker scripts/track_detections.py yes silently skipped n/a n/a Eval sidecar builder scripts/build_eval_sidecars.py yes yes writes bbox: null; the centre is not copied skipped (ball tags only) Eval harness ball_eval/dataset.py yes yes the only reader that uses the centre n/a

The hazard is latent today: none of the 45 files in ball_gt_marks has a list bbox (checked 2026-11-08). The only list values are the centres in mancity_seg104.jsonl, which is not a box sidecar. The first list-bbox file that reaches ingest_gt will stop the run (T-14).

Environment variables: FOOTY_CLIPS_DIR, FOOTY_GT_MARKS_DIR, FOOTY_BALL_CANDIDATES_DIR, FOOTY_MAX_CLIPS, FOOTY_DEBUG. The data plane is the footy data directory: ~/footy/footy_data by default, wherever the variables point otherwise (see Datasets and labels).

docs.title: 7. Known seams and risks
docs.text:
Severity: H silently corrupts training data or GT; M wrong results or lost work in a foreseeable workflow; L friction. Item ids link to the TODO list.

# Sev Seam Where TODO S1 H The labeller session drops human_checked: it keeps only label and provenance on load and writes [label, model] on flush, so one edit in a clip turns every tier-2 box in it into tier 3. No test covers it. session.py:156-161, 309-317; ingest_gt.py:191-195 T-01 S2 H Ball Check verdicts are not consumed. ingest_gt globs top-level *.jsonl only, and the export keeps not_ball and box_off boxes as positives (it filters on canonical, not on review status). ingest_gt.py:279; export_training_dataset.py:91-128 T-02 S3 H Clip identity is not canonical. The same footage has up to three stems (mancity_seg050, arsenal_mancity_seg050, arsenal_mancity_20250925_seg050); the eval exclusion and by-clip split use exact names, so eval footage can reach training and one clip can sit in both train and val. ball_check.py:709-728; export_training_dataset.py:78-80, 362-368, 385-387 T-03 S4 H Re-ingest leaves ghost rows: _upsert never deletes, and all gt_import_* runs of a clip are one canonical group, so the old row stays canonical next to the corrected box. store.py:197-220; schema.py:40-48; review.py:312-370 T-04 S5 M Undoing a corrected card appends a tombstone but leaves the box written by save_box; re-correcting appends a second box. ball_check.html:351-365; ball_check.py:771-793 T-05 S6 M Concurrent writers clobber each other: the session flush rewrites the whole sidecar from memory; review and ball_check rewrite or append to it; review's rewrites are not atomic. session.py:252-301; review.py:344, 367 T-05 S7 M Box identity is positional ((source, clip, frame, box_index)), so deletes or reordering repoint old verdicts. ball_check.py:135-149; candidates.py:17-20 T-04 S8 M The reviewed column has no consumer; tier-3 machine rows export by default, and --sources is the only tier control. export_training_dataset.py:32-34, 91-128 T-02 S9 M run_id cannot separate machines: ingest_gt hardcodes gt_import_<prov>, so two machines' sidecars overwrite each other. ingest_gt.py:197, 253 T-04 S10 M OPEN-3: provenance of vittrack reported as labeller in review. review.py:54-57, 104-108 T-14 S11 M Producers not in git: RT-DETR batch inference, ball row filter, RT-DETR training command, clip-alias symlinks (ballcheck_clips/). section 2 diagram T-09 S12 M No committed eval for the production detector. The only eval GT clip, eval_data/clips/mancity_seg104.jsonl, has no MP4 next to it, and the bake-off used the 640 checkpoint. eval_data/clips/ T-10 S13 L Unknown-tag fallbacks disagree: session in_play_ball (session.py:156), review player (review.py:102), ingest_gt the raw tag (ingest_gt.py:141). Session drops boxes on a no_ball frame; ingest_gt imports them. as cited T-14 S14 L Ball Check remaining subtracts rows from events (ball_check.py:289). S15 L A verdict POST failure ({ok: false}) is silently dropped by the page. ball_check.html:289-308 T-05 S16 L --legacy-all-reviewed stamps everything reviewed; harmless only while reviewed is unused. ingest_gt.py:314-322

Outputs nothing consumes: ball_checks/ verdicts, identity_labels/ (except the clusters view), link_proposals/, tracklets/ (identity pages only), the reviewed column, difficulty.flag_for_review, and the 2.77M machine labels (except as the Ball Check pool).

Test gaps at stage boundaries: no CI runs tests (T-08); no sidecar-to-store test; no session round-trip test for human_checked; no test that a verdict affects the store or export; no test for clip-alias leakage, for re-ingest after a correction, for undo of corrected, for concurrent flushes, or for list-bbox sidecars. 22 labeller requirements are marked UNTESTED-FRONTEND.

docs.title: Dead and unwired code
docs.text:
"Unwired" means no script, server route or pipeline stage on a live path imports it. Checked by searching imports on main, 2026-11-08; "tests only" means the only importers are in tests/. Removal is tracked as T-16 (dead code) and T-17 (scaffolds); /ingest is T-18.

Item What it was for Status labeller/app.py, labeller/_canvas_compat.py, scripts/run_labeller.py, streamlit dependencies The first, Streamlit labeller Replaced by the FastAPI labeller. Only its own run script and tests reach it. Sam3VideoLabeller, _default_model_uri (an iCloud path, labeller/video_utils.py:111-121) SAM3 video backend Re-exported by labeller/__init__.py, but the server uses VitTrack. Docstring says "kept for reference". labeller/motion_tracker.py::MotionGuidedTracker Motion-guided ball tracker Not wired. Only its Box and Detection types are imported; tests otherwise. ball_trackers/roi_yolo.py, scripts/run_bakeoff.py Ball-tracker bake-off Only the bake-off reaches them, and its results are invalid (640 px checkpoint). projection/, output/, input/streams.py, metaflow/ Serving, pitch projection, output, orchestration Scaffolds. Tests only; metaflow/ holds a Dockerfile and no flow. footy_track/logging.py, footy_track:main Logging helper, console entry point No importer; main prints "Hello from footy-track!". labelling.py, scripts/upload_classifier_frames.py, scripts/upload_object_detector_frames.py, scripts/create_roboflow_v11.py One-off Roboflow upload helpers Tests only for labelling.py; the scripts are run by hand and nothing calls them. trackers/ultralytics.py, trackers/writer.py, scripts/track_objects.py ByteTrack and BoT-SORT path Superseded by LapTracker; re-runs detection and has never been scored against GT. feature_store/difficulty.py, identity/stable_id.py Review-flag scorer; content-hash detection ids Exported and tested, but no stage calls them (detection_id is still positional). .playwright-mcp/ Browser logs Committed by accident; nothing reads them. /ingest page Clip ingestion UI The route exists but labeller/web/ingest.html does not, so it returns 500.

classifier.get_current_best_guess_classifier() silently falls back to random labels if the checkpoint fails to load (classifier.py:30-33), loads at import time (:148), and hardcodes device="mps" (:128).

Duplicated helpers (T-14): box numbering in review._read_all_boxes, review._iter_frame_box_lines and ball_check._sidecar_ball_boxes; ball label sets in four places; provenance tag sets in three (human_checked is known only to ingest_gt); video lookup by stem in three places; the crop window in review and ball_check.

Hardcoded paths (T-19): .dvc/config:4; scripts/run_bakeoff.py:26,28; labeller/video_utils.py:121; labeller/server.py:97-106 (iCloud GT fallback); feature_store/ingest_gt.py:6-7 docstring (a machine-specific example path); scripts/export_training_dataset.py:179-212,509; scripts/embed_ball_candidates.py:18-20; scripts/score_links.py:167-171; eval_data/clips/*.mp4 (40 absolute symlinks); classifier.py:128.

April docs: approach.md, problem.md, doc_review.md, ball_tracker_failure_analysis.md, system_design.md, pipelines.md and the SAM3-era labeller designs Historical; bakeoff_results.json and the failure analysis rest on the 640px checkpoint.

docs.title: 10. Open questions
docs.text:
1. Is per-player identity needed downstream, or are team and role enough? Cheap to answer, and could delete the most expensive unsolved workstream (pipeline_overview.md).
  2. What is the ball detector's number at the served resolution, on a split that spans matches? See T-10.
  3. What replaces VitTrack for the ball? A ByteTrack-style second pass over the stored conf 0.1+ detections is inference-only; see Best pipeline.
  4. What are LapTracker's purity and ID-switch rates? Only fragmentation has been measured.
  5. Does a ReID-trained embedding separate same-team players across gaps longer than 0.5 s?
  6. Can any of this be reproduced from the repo? Not today (T-09).
  7. Generalisation: every corpus-level number comes from one match.

docs.title: Ball Tracker Failure Analysis
docs.text: Date: 2026-06-21 Bead: ft-55d.1 Clips: 2 broadcast clips, 500 total sampled frames Method: YOLO detector (best checkpoint) + Hungarian LAP tracker, 250 sampled frames per clip at native 25fps

docs.title: TL;DR
docs.text: Detection failure is the dominant problem (100% of missed-ball frames). The tracker is not the bottleneck.

docs.title: Clips Analysed
docs.text: Clip Duration Frames Sampled Ball Detected Ball Tracked Missed arsenal_mancity_20250925_part192.mp4 30s 250 90 (36%) 90 (36%) 160 (64%) arsenal_mancity_example_video.mp4 10s 250 18 (7%) 18 (7%) 232 (93%) Total 500 108 (21.6%) 108 (21.6%) 392 (78.4%)

docs.title: Failure Characterisation
docs.text:
Of 392 missed-ball frames (frames where the tracker emitted no ball detection):

Failure Mode Count % of Missed Detection failure (YOLO conf = 0) 392 100% Tracker failure (detected ≥ 0.3 but dropped) 0 0% Low-conf detections dropped (0 < conf < 0.3) 0 0%

Every missed-ball frame was a detection failure — YOLO returned no ball box at all. The LapTracker dropped zero ball detections that YOLO found above threshold.

docs.title: Track ID Continuity
docs.text:
Clip Unique Ball Track IDs Track ID Switches part192 (30s, sampled at 3fps) 82 unique IDs 46 switches example_video (10s, sampled at 1fps) 6 unique IDs 8 switches

Track ID fragmentation is severe in part192: 82 unique track IDs across 90 tracked frames means the ball is almost never maintained across gaps. However, this is a consequence of detection failures, not an independent tracker failure — when detection resumes after a gap, the tracker correctly spawns a new track (IoU linking can't bridge multi-frame gaps where the ball was never seen).

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text: Root cause: YOLO detection. The ball is simply not detected in ~64–93% of frames depending on the clip. The LapTracker works correctly on every frame where YOLO returns a detection.

docs.title: Recommended Remediation Priority
docs.text:
1. Improve detection (highest priority):
  2. Lower confidence threshold below 0.3 — the analysis used 0.3 but the ball may have sub-threshold confidence in many frames
  3. Fine-tune the YOLO checkpoint on harder ball-visible frames (occlusions, motion blur, small ball)

  4. Investigate whether the two clips differ so much (36% vs 7% detection rate) due to ball visibility, camera angle, or out-of-play frames

  5. Track interpolation / Kalman smoothing (secondary):

  6. Once detection rate improves, ID switching will reduce naturally

  7. A Kalman predictor or ByteTrack-style second-pass on low-conf detections could bridge short gaps where the ball is briefly sub-threshold

  8. Tracker algorithm replacement (lower priority):

  9. The current LapTracker is not the failure point — replacing it with ByteTrack/SORT would not recover missed-ball frames since there are no detections to link

docs.text:
• runs/ball_tracker_analysis.json — full per-frame records + summaries
  • scripts/analyse_ball_tracker.py — rerunnable analysis script

docs.title: How to contribute to the docs
docs.text:
This page is for anyone who changes footy-track: people and coding agents. It says where docs live, how to change them, and how to check your work. Read it before you open a pull request (PR). A PR is a request to merge your branch into main.

The rule in one line: if your change would make a page wrong, fix the page in the same PR.

docs.title: 1. The workflow
docs.text:
The docs are plain Markdown files in docs/. A tool called MkDocs turns them into a website. When a change reaches main, GitHub builds the site and publishes it to GitHub Pages.

flowchart TD
  classDef step fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#111
  classDef auto fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#6b7280,color:#111
  A["Change code or data"]:::step --> B["Which page does it touch?<br/>(see section 2)"]:::step
  B --> C["Edit the page, or add a new one"]:::step
  C --> D["Build and look at it locally<br/>(see section 5)"]:::step
  D --> E["Open a PR with code and docs together"]:::step
  E --> F["Review and merge to main"]:::step
  F --> G["GitHub builds and publishes<br/>to GitHub Pages"]:::auto

Legend: blue boxes are things you do; the grey box happens by itself. The diagram shows the steps from changing code to a published page.

docs.title: 2. Where does my change go?
docs.text:
Ask what changed, then follow the arrow.

flowchart LR
  Q{"What did you change?"}
  Q -->|"How the system fits together,<br/>a new stage, a known problem"| ARCH["architecture.md"]
  Q -->|"Where data lives, a new dataset,<br/>label counts"| DATA["data.md"]
  Q -->|"A measured result, a model<br/>comparison, label needs"| PL["pipeline-and-labels.md"]
  Q -->|"The feature store tables<br/>or importers"| FS["design/feature_store.md"]
  Q -->|"How to train, trainer options,<br/>a training run"| TR["training.md or<br/>training/notable_runs.md"]
  Q -->|"A plan or research for<br/>something not built yet"| DES["a page under design/"]
  Q -->|"Setup, tools, how to work<br/>on the repo"| DEV["development.md"]
  Q -->|"A task started, finished<br/>or newly found"| TODO["todo.md"]
  Q -->|"None of these"| NEW["Add a new page<br/>(see section 4)"]

The diagram sends each kind of change to one page. If a change fits two pages, put the detail in one and link to it from the other. Do not copy the same table twice.

docs.title: 3. The site map
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  ROOT["Docs site"] --> OV["Overview<br/>start here"]
  ROOT --> AR["Architecture<br/>what is wired, what is broken"]
  ROOT --> PL["Pipeline and labels<br/>best results, label needs"]
  ROOT --> DA["Data<br/>datasets, labels, footage"]
  ROOT --> TRN["Training<br/>how to train, past runs"]
  ROOT --> FS["Feature store<br/>the annotation database"]
  ROOT --> DS["Design<br/>plans and research"]
  ROOT --> DV["Development<br/>setup, agents, this guide"]
  ROOT --> TD["TODO<br/>the only task list"]

The map shows the top-level sections of the site and what each one is for. The order matches nav: in mkdocs.yml.

docs.title: 4. Add a page
docs.text:
1. Create docs/<name>.md. Use lower-case words, with - or _ between them. Match the pages near it.
  2. Start with one # heading. Add one sentence under it saying who the page is for and why they would read it.
  3. Add one line to nav: in mkdocs.yml, under the right section: - Title: file-name.md.
  4. Link to it from at least one other page. A page nothing links to is hard to find.
  5. Build the site (section 5). The build prints a list of pages that are not in the nav. Yours must not be on it.

Do not edit pyproject.toml or uv.lock to add docs tools.

docs.title: 5. Build and preview
docs.text:
From the repo root:

uvx --with mkdocs-material mkdocs build -d /tmp/footy-site

This builds the site into /tmp/footy-site without changing the repo. Read the warnings. Do not add new ones. (--strict currently fails on two old links in system_design.md; that is known.)

For a live preview, run uvx --with mkdocs-material mkdocs serve. It serves the site on http://127.0.0.1:8000 and reloads when you save.

docs.title: 6. Writing style
docs.text:
Write for a smart person who is new to the project.

  • Short, plain sentences. Say "use" and not "utilise". If you need a technical word, explain it the first time.
  • Say who the page is for in the first lines.
  • Lead with what and why. Put the answer first. Put the detail after it.
  • One idea per paragraph.
  • Give an example when a rule is abstract. A command, a table row or a path is better than a description.
  • Use tables for reference material (options, paths, counts). Use sentences for reasoning.
  • Link to code by file path, for example src/footy_track/labeller/session.py. Add a line number only when it really matters. Line numbers go stale quickly.
  • Say what is measured and what is assumed. Write "measured" with its source, or "unverified". Do not mix them.
  • Date numbers that go stale, for example "18,147 objects (2026-11-08)".
  • No marketing words and no filler.

docs.title: 7. Diagrams
docs.text:
Draw diagrams in Mermaid. Mermaid is text that the site turns into a picture, so a diagram is reviewed like code. Put it in a fenced block that starts with ```mermaid.

Pick the type by the job:

Job Use Data flow or steps flowchart Who calls whom, in order sequenceDiagram Something with states, such as a label going from draft to checked stateDiagram-v2 A choice with branches flowchart with a {} decision box

Rules:

  • Keep it small. About 15 nodes at most. If it is bigger, split it into two diagrams.
  • Use the shared colours from the architecture page. Define them with classDef: grey is data on disk or S3, blue is code in git, orange with a dashed border is a step that is not in git, red is dead code or an output nothing reads, purple is new.
  • Quote every label: A["Some label"].
  • Break lines with <br/>, not with a newline.
  • Escape special characters. Write & for &, < for < and > for >. Avoid #, ; and unbalanced quotes in labels.
  • Add a one-line legend under the diagram for the colours you used.
  • Add one sentence under the diagram saying what it shows. This is the text for people who cannot see the picture.

A tiny example that follows the rules:

flowchart LR
  classDef code fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#111
  classDef data fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#6b7280,color:#111
  V[("Match video")]:::data --> S["Segmenter"]:::code --> C[("Shot clips")]:::data

Legend: grey is data, blue is code in git. The diagram shows a video going through the segmenter into shot clips.

docs.title: 8. Check that a diagram renders
docs.text:
A diagram with a syntax error shows an error box or nothing. Always look at it.

  1. Build the site: uvx --with mkdocs-material mkdocs build -d /tmp/footy-site.
  2. Serve it: cd /tmp/footy-site && python3 -m http.server 8911.
  3. Open the page in a headless browser and take a screenshot. With Playwright (a browser-driving tool) for Node.js:
const { chromium } = require('playwright');
(async () => {
  const b = await chromium.launch({
    executablePath: process.env.HOME + '/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-1140/chrome-linux/chrome',
    args: ['--no-sandbox'] });
  const p = await b.newPage({ viewport: { width: 1300, height: 900 } });
  await p.goto('http://localhost:8911/contributing-docs/', { waitUntil: 'networkidle' });
  await p.waitForTimeout(8000);
  await p.locator('.mermaid').nth(0).screenshot({ path: 'diagram0.png' });
  await b.close();
})();
  1. Open the PNG and look at it. Do this for every diagram you added or changed.

Two things to know:

  • Material draws Mermaid inside a closed shadow DOM, so document.querySelectorAll('.mermaid svg') finds nothing even when the picture is fine. Check the screenshot, not the page structure.
  • The Mermaid script loads from a CDN (a public file host). The browser needs internet access.

Optional: make docs-check runs scripts/check_docs_diagrams.py (a quick text check for empty diagrams, unbalanced quotes, loose & or <, and diagrams over 25 nodes) and then the build. It is not run in CI yet.

docs.title: 9. What must never go in the docs
docs.text:
The repo and the site (https://egroeg121.github.io/footy-track/) are public. Anyone can read every page and every old version in git history.

Never write:

  • Keys, tokens or passwords of any kind.
  • Private hostnames, IP addresses or Tailscale names.
  • Cloud bucket names, account ids, or full private paths beyond what the page needs.
  • Personal data: emails, phone numbers, names of people in footage who are not public figures.
  • Screenshots of private tools (cloud consoles, dashboards, chats).

Write this instead:

Instead of Write A full home or disk path "the data directory" and name the setting that points to it, for example FOOTY_GT_MARKS_DIR A bucket name "the private S3 bucket" A machine name "the workstation" or "the GPU box" A key "set WANDB_API_KEY in your environment" (the name, never the value)

If you find one already in the docs, remove it and tell the owner. A leaked secret must also be revoked: deleting it from the page does not delete it from git history.

docs.title: 10. Agents
docs.text:
An agent is an AI coding tool working from a brief. Agents follow the same rules. The steps are:

sequenceDiagram
  participant H as Person
  participant A as Agent
  participant R as Repo and docs
  participant B as Build and browser
  H->>A: Brief
  A->>R: Read contributing-docs.md and the pages the brief touches
  A->>R: Change the code
  A->>R: Update the docs and todo.md in the same change
  A->>B: Build the site
  A->>B: Screenshot each new or changed diagram
  B-->>A: Warnings and picture
  A->>R: Commit and push a branch
  A->>H: Open or offer a PR, with the checklist filled in

The diagram shows an agent reading the docs first, changing code and docs together, checking the build and the pictures, and only then pushing.

docs.title: Datasets and labels
docs.text:
Who this is for: anyone who needs to find, count or trust the footy data and its labels. It says where each dataset lives, what a label is worth (tiers), how the evaluation sets are built, and what exists on one machine but not the other.

Counts measured on 2026-11-08 on the build machine against main @ 26d2506. They will drift; re-run the checks before relying on them. Figures marked "inventory" come from the review's dataset inventory and were not recounted. For how the data moves through the system see Architecture; for what is missing see the TODO list.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text:
All paths below are relative to the footy data directory. It is not in git. Its location differs per machine, so code reads it from environment variables or a per-user default.

Place Contents Footy data directory on the build machine (45 GB, 18,716 files) The working copy of everything below. ~/code/footy_data On the build machine, a dangling symlink into iCloud left over from the macOS setup. Do not use. The object store, under a footy_data/ prefix 18,147 objects, 47.88 GB. Sibling prefixes gpu_runs/ (18 objects, 795 MB), models/ (3 objects, 67 MB) and backups/. The desktop GPU machine A third copy, about 44 GB per the maintainer's notes. Not checked in this review. The notes record the two machines diverging on ball_gt_marks in August; not verified. ~/footy/footy_data Where the labeller looks by default. Override with FOOTY_CLIPS_DIR, FOOTY_GT_MARKS_DIR and FOOTY_BALL_CANDIDATES_DIR (labeller/server.py:92-114). A separate data folder next to the repo Only arsenal_mancity_example_video.mp4 (1920x1080, 25 fps, 250 frames, 10 s).

Model weights are not in git. rtdetr_1920_v11/best.pt (66.8 MB) is in the object store under models/ and gpu_runs/, and on the build machine. The SAM3 weights go in model_saves/sam3/; the object store has the complete sam3.1_multiplex.pt, the local copy is a partial download.

docs.title: Label tiers and provenance tags
docs.text:
A label is worth what the person or program behind it is worth. Every box in a sidecar file carries tags in the order [class, provenance, *markers], and the tiers are read from those tags (labeller/README.md section 1; feature_store/ingest_gt.py:73-77, 93-115).

Tier Tags on the box What it means In the feature store For training 1 labeller A human drew or dragged this box. source = hand_label, reviewed = true Ground truth. Safe to train and evaluate on. 2 vittrack plus human_checked A tracker drew the box and a human confirmed it. About 97% right on the 81 Ball Check verdicts over such boxes (measured, 2026-11-08). source = vittrack, reviewed = true once the ingest fix is in the store Good enough to train on. Not good enough as strict eval ground truth. 3 yolo, sam3, or vittrack without human_checked; also every machine label from RT-DETR A machine drew it and nobody looked. reviewed = false Noisy. Below 0.6 detector confidence at most 42% of Ball Check cards were real balls (precision bands).

Three details that trip people up:

  • human_checked is a marker, not a provenance and not a class. It sits after the provenance tag. Before ingest_gt knew this, it read the marker as the object class and lost the real one.
  • No code in the repo writes human_checked (searched 2026-11-08). The 15,386 vittrack rows that carry it got it from a one-off backfill on 2026-08-23. New VitTrack output cannot become tier 2 through any tool.
  • The labeller session currently drops human_checked on load and flush, which silently turns tier 2 into tier 3 for a whole clip (T-01; the fix is on an unmerged branch).

docs.title: Label formats and counts
docs.text:
Sidecar rows are {frame_index, bbox{x,y,w,h} normalised, center, tags: [class, provenance, *markers]}; skip markers are rows with bbox: null and tag no_ball or not_broadcast. See Architecture, section 6 for the six formats.

Current ball_gt_marks (45 files, 22,648 rows, 0 unparsable; measured 2026-11-08): player 18,688, referee 2,099, in_play_ball 1,523, not_broadcast 138 (marker), coach 81, no_ball 68 (marker), person 32, player_sub 13, out_of_play_ball 2, untagged 4.

Ball provenance tiers: tier 1 labeller 692 (plus 2 out_of_play_ball); tier 2 vittrack plus human_checked 825; tier 3 yolo 6. vittrack rows total 15,386, all carrying human_checked; labeller rows 6,446; yolo 606. An older note's 612/857/6 matches the August feature store, not these files.

Verdicts (364 rows): ball 179, not_ball 149, unsure 20, corrected 12, tombstones 4. By source: 283 candidates, 81 sidecar boxes. Machine labels: player 2,028,121; in_play_ball 352,039; referee 285,162; coach 53,607; person 26,463; player_sub 16,986; ball 4,773 (class ball is dead in Roboflow v11 but present in machine output).

Roboflow v11 in_play_ball instances, counted per file: train 1,010, valid 211, test 243. (cat labels/*.txt undercounts because the files lack a trailing newline; an older figure of 826 for train was that miscount.) v11-val is 74% one clip, arsenal_example.

docs.title: Evaluation sets
docs.text:
There are two, and neither is a multi-match benchmark. Both are defined by files, so check the files before quoting a score.

Set Defined by Size Limits Roboflow v11-val (single-frame ball detection) detection_dataset/roboflow_dataset_11/valid 215 images, 211 in_play_ball 157 images and 156 balls (74%) are one 10-second clip, arsenal_example. Counted from file names, 2026-11-08. The production checkpoint's headline figure (mAP50 0.665, recall 0.591) is measured here. Roboflow v11-test detection_dataset/roboflow_dataset_11/test 268 images, 243 in_play_ball Never evaluated in any log found. 265 of the 268 images (241 of 243 balls) are frames cut from the full Man City match video, not from clips, so it is one match. Counted from file names, 2026-11-08. Ball-tracker harness set (ball_eval) Every clip with a <stem>.jsonl sidecar in eval_data/clips/ One file, mancity_seg104.jsonl: 4 rows, all with the same centre, and no matching MP4 Effectively empty. The bake-off that used it ran the ball-blind 640 px checkpoint, so its results are not valid (Architecture, section 4.1).

The harness set doubles as the leakage guard: export_training_dataset excludes every clip that has a sidecar in eval_data/clips/ from train and val (scripts/export_training_dataset.py:78-80, 362-363). It matches clip names exactly, and one clip has up to three names, so the guard can miss (T-03). The split in v11 itself is by clip, but v11 train, val and test are all mostly Man City (v11 train has 1,010 balls, 517 of them from astonvilla_seg080).

What a better set needs (diverse matches, dense contiguous frames, explicit no_ball frames) is in Best pipeline and label needs, section 3.

docs.title: Local versus the object store
docs.text:
Counts from a listing on 2026-11-08 (measured). The top-level folders marked in the layout diagram are the ones that differ.

In both Object store only Local only Keys 18,112 3 604 What Clips, machine labels, GT sidecars including ball_checks/ (same file sizes on both sides as of 2026-09-25), Roboflow datasets _backups/ball_gt_marks_2026-07-04, the complete sam3.1_multiplex.pt, roboflow_dataset_11/test/labels.cache ball_candidates, ball_embeddings, tracklets, the GT snapshots, identity_labels, link_proposals, track_videos, the partial SAM3 file, both feature stores

Practical rules:

  • Ball Check needs ball_candidates/ and ball_embeddings/, which are local only. A new machine has to rebuild them from machine_labels/ with a filter script that is not in git (T-09).
  • The labeller and ball_check read sidecars from FOOTY_GT_MARKS_DIR. Two machines writing to different copies is how the August divergence happened.
  • The object store credentials work; an older note saying they were dead (2026-08-26) is stale.

docs.title: Gaps
docs.text:
• Footage without labels: Norwich and Bournemouth 2nd half have no GT. Machine labels cover only the 162 Man City clips. See Best pipeline and label needs for which gaps matter (T-13).
  • Labels without footage: arsenal_example (3,348 rows, 176 ball marks) has only the 10 s example video, tied by name. eval_data/clips/mancity_seg104.jsonl has no MP4.
  • Not in the feature store: see Feature store design, section 7.1 (T-07).
  • Format hazards: two centre formats (dict and list) can still appear; ball_gt_marks has 4 untagged rows; astonvilla_seg080.jsonl differs from its backup because six vittrack boxes were rewritten as labeller by the corrected path, so Ball Check does rewrite sidecars.
  • Cross-machine: rows that exist only on the desktop GPU machine cannot be checked from the build machine.

docs.title: Data Formats
docs.text: This document describes the expected directory layouts for raw match data and Roboflow training datasets, and the environment variables required by the training scripts.

docs.title: Raw match layout
docs.text:
Match data lives under data/ and is organised by match name:

data/
└── <match_name>/               # e.g. arsenal_mancity
    ├── original_video/         # source video file(s) for the match
    │   └── *.mp4               # one file per half / recording chunk
    └── full_video_frames/      # frames extracted from the source video
        └── *.jpg               # one image per extracted frame (default JPEG)

docs.title: original_video/
docs.text: Contains the raw .mp4 recording(s) for a single match. Long recordings should be split into chunks first using split_video.py (see src/footy_track/scripts/README.md); the resulting parts are stored here.

docs.title: full_video_frames/
docs.text:
Contains the per-frame images produced by extract_frames.py. Default format is JPEG at 1 FPS; PNG and WEBP are also supported.

# Extract frames from a source video into the expected directory
uv run footy-track-extract-frames \
    data/arsenal_mancity/original_video/match.mp4 \
    --outdir data/arsenal_mancity/full_video_frames

Frames can optionally carry EXIF metadata (--embed-metadata):

EXIF tag Content video_id Match identifier string frame_index Zero-based frame number timestamp_seconds Wall-clock position in the source video

Matches used in practice (referenced in notebooks):

Match Directory name Arsenal vs Manchester City arsenal_mancity Arsenal vs Norwich arsenal_norwich Arsenal vs Aston Villa arsenal_astonvilla Arsenal vs Bournemouth (1st half) arsenal_bournmouth_1st_half Arsenal vs Bournemouth (2nd half) arsenal_bournmouth_2nd_half

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Variable Required Description ROBOFLOW_API_KEY Yes Roboflow API key. Used by all training scripts and upload utilities to authenticate against the Roboflow API. Obtain it from your Roboflow workspace settings.

The Roboflow SDK also reads the key from ~/.config/roboflow/config.json if you have previously run roboflow login.

Training metrics are logged to Weights & Biases if the wandb CLI is authenticated (wandb login). No explicit env var is required beyond the standard WANDB_API_KEY that the W&B SDK reads automatically.

docs.title: Development Guide
docs.text: This guide covers how to set up, develop, and work with the Footy Scan codebase.

docs.title: Setting Up Development Environment
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository: 

    git clone <repository-url>
cd football-scan

  2. Python Environment: We use uv for Python environment and dependency management. First, install uv if you haven't already: 

    curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

  3. Install the package in development mode: 

    uv pip install -e .

  4. Install additional dependencies for ML and video processing (if needed): 

    uv pip install "torch" "opencv-python" "tqdm"

docs.title: Using the Makefile (recommended)
docs.text:
Common repo-wide tasks are captured in the Makefile to standardize workflows:

make setup make deps-update

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
We use MkDocs with the Material theme for documentation. To work with docs:

# Serve docs locally (with live reload)
uv run mkdocs serve

# Build the documentation site
uv run mkdocs build

# Deploy to GitHub Pages (if configured)
uv run mkdocs gh-deploy

The documentation will be available at http://127.0.0.1:8000 when serving locally.

docs.title: Running Tests
docs.text:
uv run pytest        # everything (also: make tests)
make test-fast       # skips tests marked slow or needs_weights

Tests marked needs_weights skip themselves when the model weights (e.g. model_saves/sam3/sam3.pt) have not been pulled from DVC/LFS.

The project uses two main time formats: - ContinuousTime: Continuous seconds from game start - GameTime: Referee/broadcast clock time

The processing pipeline consists of three main components: - InputConsumer: Video frame input - Processor: Detection and tracking - OutputProducer: Data serialization

See Pipeline Architecture for detailed design information.

docs.text: When using automated tools or agents with this codebase, follow the guidelines in Agent Guidelines to maintain consistency.

docs.title: Docs
docs.text: To change the docs, read How to contribute to the docs.

docs.title: Environment notes
docs.text:
Who this is for: anyone setting up a new machine, especially an older or unusual one. These notes were measured on the review's build machine on 2026-11-08.

  • Old CPUs without AVX2 crash on import. The build machine's CPU lacks AVX2. The newest duckdb and the stock polars die with an illegal instruction there. The workaround is duckdb==1.3.2 and polars-lts-cpu in the virtual environment only. pyproject.toml asks for duckdb>=1.5.3, and polars arrives through ultralytics; do not edit pyproject.toml or uv.lock to work around a local CPU.
  • Open the feature store read-only when inspecting it: duckdb.connect(path, read_only=True). See Feature store design, section 7.1.
  • Weights are not in git. model_saves/sam3/sam3.pt and the detector checkpoints come from the object store or DVC/LFS. Tests that need them fail without the file (see below).
  • No GPU is needed for the tests. No test uses CUDA (checked 2026-11-08). The slow ones are model tests that run on the CPU.
  • Where the data is is covered in Datasets and labels; the labeller finds it through FOOTY_CLIPS_DIR, FOOTY_GT_MARKS_DIR and FOOTY_BALL_CANDIDATES_DIR.

docs.title: Running the tests
docs.text:
The suite has 462 tests (collected 2026-11-08). The whole run took about 4 m 30 s before the speed-up and about 52 s after it (measured on the build machine, same date).

Why it was slow. The guess was a GPU problem. It was not: no test uses CUDA. Three things took almost all the time: two SAM3 tests (about 75 to 80 s each, and they fail anyway when the weights file is missing) and the first fiftyone test (about 17 s of start-up).

What fixes it. The chore/faster-tests changes are merged (with PR #24). You get:

Command What runs Time (measured before the merge) uv run pytest or make tests Everything about 52 s make test-fast Skips tests marked slow or needs_weights about 25 s

The needs_weights marker is for tests that need model weights that are not in the repo; they skip themselves when the file is missing. The change also makes the extract_frames test fixture create its output folder first, because ffmpeg does not.

  FAST["make test-fast<br/>about 25 s"]:::new

  FO["fiftyone tests<br/>about 17 s start-up<br/>slow"]:::new
  W[("sam3.pt weights<br/>not in git")]:::data

  ALL --> SAM
  ALL --> FO
  FAST -. "skips" .-> SAM
  FAST -. "skips" .-> FO
